text:
maya: quick sync — we need to finalize how legacy API keys without scope fields get mapped into our new RBAC model. hit a couple of UX and runtime tradeoffs.
chris: what are the options again? full auto-classify vs opt-in migration endpoints?
olga: summary: (A) auto-classify and attach `scope_hint` + notify owners, (B) issue ephemeral scoped tokens via exchange (recommended for svc-to-svc), (C) require owners to create new scoped tokens and sunset legacy keys.
sam: prefer B for services and A for human-owned keys to avoid breaking dashboards. But we should be explicit about permission widening risk with heuristics.
maya: agreed. classification heuristics we discussed: 1) project_id column -> project scope, 2) email domain or billing_owner -> org scope, 3) token name patterns (svc-, cron-, infra-) -> service, 4) last-used < 90d and no owner -> orphaned -> mark for deprovision.
olch: (note: olga) add rule: keys used only by internal infra LBs -> org-service hybrid (restrict to internal endpoints).
chris: runtime behavior: if key has no explicit scope, treat as `legacy` and consult `scope_hint` if present. If hint absent, deny high-privilege operations (admin/billing change) by default. Emit metric `auth.legacy_key_called` and increment `auth.legacy_privileged_attempts` on blocked ops.
maya: performance note: do not perform DB join per-request. add `scope_hint` column on api_keys table and populate via batch job. runtime caches hints in memcache with TTL 5m and warm on startup. invalidation on rotate.
sam: security: we need audit entries that show original key id + assigned scope_hint so we can trace misclassifications. log format: `legacy_migration:{key_id}->{scope_hint}:{classifier}`.
olga: Exchange API design (for svc): POST /v1/token/exchange {grant_type=legacy_key, subject=scoped_audience} => returns short-lived JWT (1h) with scoped claims. Rate limit exchanges per key (e.g., 100/day) and require mTLS for high-priv scopes.
chris: migration policy timeline: 1) Inventory + classification (2 weeks), 2) Scoped token onboarding + exchange endpoint -> soft-start (canary 5% traffic) (4 weeks), 3) Deprecation warnings + reminders (30/60/90 days), 4) enforcement (120 days).
maya: owners: inventory job -> maya, classification heuristics doc -> olga, exchange RFC -> chris, metrics/dashboards -> sam.
sam: dashboards: legacy_keys_total, legacy_keys_active, exchange_count, exchange_rate_limited, orphaned_keys. Also add a per-key migration_progress tag for exports.
olga: noticed edge-case: third-party integrators embed keys in UI assets (public). propose a separate public-key-check and immediate rotate strategy + notify security team.
maya: agree. we'll surface `public_key_risk` in inventory and escalate.
chris: question: do we allow `X-Original-Key` header during migration? pros: eases client update. cons: increases risk vector. 
sam: if we allow it, restrict to 90-day window, log every use, and require the exchange endpoint to be the recommended path. rate-limit heavily.
maya: final call: allow `X-Original-Key` for 90 days, but default canary enforcement will reject legacy keys on 95% of traffic once enforcement flag flips. we'll start with 5% enforcement (canary) then 25/50/95.
deploy-bot: scheduled: feature-flag `auth.legacy-scope-migration` will be created in staging 2026-04-05T08:00Z.
chris: follow-ups: I'll create the exchange RFC + sample cURL flows. olga: please add classification SQLs and heuristics to the doc repo. maya: i'll own rollout checklist and run the inventory job this week. sam: i'll build the dashboard and alerts for spikes in `legacy_privileged_attempts`.
maya: thanks everyone. check-in next Tue.
